subject: SIG - encryption implementation summary and rotation artifacts request
messages:
From: Lola Turner <lola.turner@acme-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-analytics.com; James Li <james.li@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: encryption artifacts needed for review

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As part of our SIG review we need a compact artifacts bundle covering encryption controls: in-transit cipher suites and TLS config, at-rest envelope encryption and KMS design, HSM custody attestations, and a rotation log for KMS keys covering 2025-2027.

Can you confirm:
- Rotation cadence for customer-facing data keys and KEKs (policy + when last rotated)
- Whether HSMs are used for KEK generation and where custody is recorded
- Any proof-of-rotation logs we can ingest (CSV preferred)

If you can provide a zip or Drive folder with a manifest and the artifacts by EOD next Friday (2027-11-12) that would be ideal. If any items are sensitive we can accept redacted PDFs.

Cheers,
Lola
Lola Turner
Security Program Manager
Acme Analytics

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption artifacts needed for review

Hi Lola —

Thanks for the clear list. I can assemble a compact package. Marcus will pull rotation logs from KeyOps; Stephanie will add the HSM custody attestations and the TLS/transit matrix.

A couple quick clarifications before we prepare the bundle:
1) For "rotation log"—do you want the operational rotation events (who triggered, timestamp, key id) or the periodic policy records (planned cadence + last action)? We can provide both, but the event log tends to be more detailed.
2) Do you need raw HSM export files (we normally provide signed attest PDFs) or is a signed attestation sufficient?

We’ll aim to drop a Drive folder and a manifest (sig_evidence_manifest_v1.pdf) by 2027-11-08. If that timeline is tight, tell us which items are highest priority.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Security (interim)
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption artifacts needed for review

Kimberly —

Quick update: KeyOps exported rotation events for customer KEKs and platform KEKs from 2025-11-01 through 2027-10-31. I sanitized principal IDs and included the event columns you asked for: key_id, event_type (rotate/create/destroy), actor, timestamp, rotation_ticket_id. CSV is attached.

Notes:
- We never export private key material. Logs include KMS key IDs (K-xxxx) and the rotation ticket reference.
- Rotation cadence: policy requires KEKs rotated annually or on significant infra changes; data keys (envelope keys) rotate per-customer or by re-encrypt windows configured by workload.

I included a short README in the package describing how to interpret the ticket IDs and mapping to our audit traces.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Key Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- kms_rotation_log_2025-2027.csv
- rotation_readme.md

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Lola Turner <lola.turner@acme-analytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: James Li <james.li@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 08:09:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption artifacts needed for review

Lola / team —

Uploading the HSM custody attestations and the transit cipher matrix now. A few implementation details inline:
- HSMs: We use FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certified HSM appliances for KEK generation and signing operations. Custody attestations (signed PDFs) include physical key ceremony dates and custodian lists.
- Key custody: dual-control procedures are logged in our custody ledger; attestations include the custody ledger excerpt (redacted where required).
- TLS/in-transit: our frontend load balancers negotiate TLS 1.2+ and prefer TLS 1.3. The attached transit_cipher_matrix.txt lists supported cipher suites and validated configurations for our public and internal endpoints.

I placed the files in 
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bSIGEvidence (restricted link — Acme security group has view access).

Attachments included in the Drive:
- hsm_custody_attestations_2026.pdf
- transit_cipher_matrix.txt
- sig_evidence_manifest_v1.pdf

Let me know if you need full raw custody exports; otherwise the signed attestations should satisfy the SIG review.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

--
[attachment: hsm_custody_attestations_2026.pdf]

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround on this review.

Subject: Re: SIG evidence bundle: encryption + rotation artifacts (link and manifest)

Kim / team —

Received, and thanks for the thorough package. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we close the SIG item:
1) For KEK rotation cadence — you mentioned annual for KEKs and per-customer for envelope keys. Can you confirm whether any KEKs rotated outside the annual cadence in the past 24 months and the triggering reason? If so, provide the rotation_ticket_id(s).
2) For the HSM custody attestations — are the custodians listed by role or full name? We can accept role-only but will need to capture a mapping in our internal audit notes.

If you can reply with the small clarifications above, we can mark the SIG question as addressed.

Best,
James Li
Security Engineer
Acme Analytics
